cases.prompt:
TASK. You are given the weights of pi0.5, a vision-language-action model (VLA) that controls a Franka robot arm in the LIBERO simulator (the released openpi checkpoint "pi05_libero", fine-tuned on the LIBERO demonstrations). Your job is to make it more ROBUST to one kind of perturbation, "Language Instructions", by EDITING ITS WEIGHTS DIRECTLY: find out what goes wrong inside the network when the perturbation makes it fail, identify the components responsible, and repair them with targeted changes, without hurting its performance on the other perturbation categories.

THE MODEL (3.62 B parameters; tensor names and shapes in NAMES / SHAPES).
- VISION: SigLIP So400m/14 ("paligemma_with_expert.paligemma.model.vision_tower.vision_model.*", 27 layers, width 1152) encodes each 224x224 camera image into 256 tokens; a linear projector ("...multi_modal_projector.linear") maps them to 2048.
- VLM: Gemma-2B ("paligemma_with_expert.paligemma.model.language_model.*", 18 layers, width 2048, 8 query heads and 1 KV head of dim 256, MLP 16384, embed_tokens 257152x2048) processes the prefix: 256 base-camera tokens, 256 wrist-camera tokens, 256 tokens of a masked-out third (empty) image, and the tokenized instruction (padded to 200 tokens). It builds a KV cache.
- ACTION EXPERT: Gemma-300M ("paligemma_with_expert.gemma_expert.model.*", 18 layers, width 1024, same head layout, MLP 4096) runs on 10 action tokens; in every layer its queries attend to the VLM's keys/values of the same layer (the prefix) and to the action tokens. Its RMSNorms are adaptive ("input_layernorm.dense", "post_attention_layernorm.dense", "norm.dense": Linear 1024->3072 conditioned on the flow-matching time). "action_in_proj", "action_out_proj", "time_mlp_in/out" map between the 32-d action space and width 1024. "gemma_expert.lm_head" is unused.
- INFERENCE: flow matching, 10 Euler steps from Gaussian noise, producing a chunk of 10 future actions (7-D: end-effector delta pose + gripper); the first 5 are executed, then the model is queried again. The robot state is NOT an input. The VLM prefix is computed once per query; the action expert reads it through attention at every denoising step.
- Inference runs in bf16 for most tensors (690 bf16, 122 fp32: layernorms, SigLIP embeddings, action heads); your edits are cast to each tensor's dtype, so changes much smaller than bf16 resolution (~0.4% relative) are lost.

THE BENCHMARK. LIBERO-Plus: the 4 LIBERO suites (spatial, object, goal, long/libero_10) with 7 perturbation categories (Camera Viewpoints, Robot Initial States, Language Instructions, Light Conditions, Background Textures, Sensor Noise, Objects Layout) and difficulty levels 1-5. An episode succeeds if the task's goal predicate holds within the step limit (220 spatial, 280 object, 300 goal, 520 libero_10). On a 700-episode sample of the practice variants this checkpoint succeeds on 86% overall; it is weakest on Camera Viewpoints at difficulty 5 (~40%) and on Language Instructions at difficulty 4-5 (~55-75%). Language Instructions variants paraphrase the task instruction (synonyms, descriptions instead of names, added context); in libero_goal, where 10 different tasks share one scene, the model often carries out the WRONG task or manipulates the wrong object for a paraphrase (e.g. "activate the cooktop" -> opens the drawer), while it succeeds on the literal instructions of the same scenes.

HOW IT WILL BE MEASURED. After you finish, the edited and the unedited model are evaluated on HELD-OUT LIBERO-Plus variants you never see (a fixed half of all variants, chosen by a hash), with fixed seeds: success rate on "Language Instructions" (the goal: raise it) and on every other category (must not drop; a drop of more than ~2 points counts against you). Only weight values change: same tensor names and shapes, same inference code and settings.

WHAT COUNTS. Edits that come from understanding the network: find what goes wrong when the perturbation causes failure (e.g. which instruction tokens and which VLM features carry the task identity, which action-expert heads read them, where a paraphrase and the literal instruction diverge), localize the responsible components causally, and change them in a way you can justify with evidence. Out of scope: training of any kind; edits that only multiply a whole tensor by a constant; global changes to the noise or action scaling that are not tied to a mechanism.

WHAT YOU HAVE.
1. A persistent Python kernel (no internet, no GPU; CPU with many cores): variables survive between code blocks, like a notebook. Reply with exactly one block that starts with ```python to run code; if its last line is an expression its value is shown. One execution may take up to 900 s and 96 GB; output is cut at 10,000 characters; at most 300 code runs. Predefined: NAMES (all editable tensor names), SHAPES, load(name) (float32 torch tensor: your current edit if any, else the original), load_original(name), save_edit(name, tensor), drop_edit(name), edited() (names you edited), WORK (your read-write folder, kept for the whole run), and BENCH (read-only): BENCH/practice_variants.json lists the PRACTICE variants (suite, id, name, category, difficulty) - the only ones you may run; the held-out ones are not listed. Gradients are disabled. The model's tokenizer is BENCH/paligemma_tokenizer.model (sentencepiece is installed: sentencepiece.SentencePieceProcessor(model_file=...)); openpi tokenizes the prompt as the cleaned instruction text followed by a newline ("\n"), with a BOS token. The instruction strings are in the rollout records; the token ranges of each query are in the probe outputs ("prefix_layout").
2. A forward-pass tool with a budget of 50 passes. Reply with exactly one block that starts with ```forward and contains JSON. Each request costs one pass:
 (a) ROLLOUT: {"type": "rollout", "model": "original" | "edited" | "both", "episodes": [{"suite": "...", "id": <practice variant id>, "seed": <int>}, ...] OR "sample": {"category": "...", "suite": optional, "difficulty": optional list, "n": <int>, "seed": <int>}, "record": optional {"vlm_layers": [...], "expert_layers": [...], "vision_layers": [...], "what": "attn_out" | "mlp_out" | "resid"}, "save_frames": optional bool}. At most 256 episodes per pass ("both": at most 128 per model, run on the same variants and seeds, returning the paired difference with its standard error). Returns success (overall, by category, suite and difficulty), steps, and failure modes; per-episode records (including the instruction) in WORK/roll_<k>.jsonl; with "record", per-episode activation summaries (mean over the episode's policy queries; VLM outputs averaged separately over base-image, wrist-image and instruction tokens, expert outputs over the action tokens) as .npy in WORK/roll_<k>_acts/ with index.json; with "save_frames", the first observation and every 50th step of each episode as .png in WORK/roll_<k>_frames/ and the exact policy inputs needed for probes.
 (b) PROBE (cheap, no simulation): {"type": "probe", "model": "original" | "edited" | "both", "inputs": "<path of saved policy inputs from a rollout with save_frames, or a list of them>", "return": {"layers": [expert layers], "vlm_layers": [...], "vision_layers": [...], "what": "attn_out" | "mlp_out" | "resid" | "attn_maps"}}: runs the policy on stored observations (up to 512 inputs) and returns the predicted action chunk and requested activations (per call) as .npy in WORK/probe_<k>/ (attention maps of the action expert over the prefix: at most 4 inputs, at most 4 layers).
A rollout pass of 256 episodes takes on the order of 10 minutes.

HOW TO WORK.
1. Diagnose first: compare rollouts on "Language Instructions" variants with less perturbed ones of the same tasks; look at how it fails (which task it performs instead, saved frames, action statistics), and at which internal features differ.
2. Localize causally: correlation between a component and success is not enough; show that changing it changes the behaviour as predicted, with a dose-response.
3. Measure with power: success over n episodes has a standard error of about 50/sqrt(n) points. Compare original and edited on the SAME variants and seeds ("model": "both"), and keep an edit only if its gain is clearly larger than its standard error on variants not used to choose it. Check other categories for damage before you finish.
4. Plan your passes; keep WORK/notes.md up to date (findings with numbers, edits tried and their measured effect, current best edit; it is shown to you again if the conversation is restarted); keep copies of good edits (e.g. copy WORK/edited to WORK/best_1/).
5. Print compact summaries, never whole arrays; outputs are ASCII only.

RULES. Not allowed: (a) gradient descent or any training (no backward passes, autograd, optimizers, or iterative fitting of weights to a loss); (b) running the network yourself in the kernel on inputs (only the forward tool runs it); (c) reading benchmark files other than BENCH/practice_variants.json (in particular not the held-out variant list) or anything outside WORK, BENCH and the weights; (d) internet access. Allowed: any analysis of weights and forward-tool results, any direct edit of weights that you compute and that is in scope.

HOW THE SESSION RUNS. It continues until all 50 forward passes are used; then make your final choice (the tensors in WORK/edited are submitted) and reply without a code block, saying what you changed, the evidence, and why you expect it to help.

cases.final_answer:
**I am submitting the frozen F edit currently in `/work/edited`.**

### What changed
Only **65 rows** of `paligemma_with_expert.paligemma.model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight` were changed: approximately **0.025% of embedding rows**.

The edit uses direct interpolation toward existing, action-grounded word embeddings, such as `cooker -> stove` and `basin -> bowl`. Ambiguous cues receive partial or centroid-based changes; for example, `dairy` is not forced exclusively toward `cheese`. Canonical instruction tokens are protected.

No vision, attention, MLP, action-expert, or action-scaling weights changed. No training was used.

### Mechanism and causal evidence
The diagnosed failures involved **incorrect task/object cues despite active attention to the instruction**. Embedding repairs shifted downstream expert representations toward successful same-task controls.

A diagnostic dose-response supported this localization:

| Edit strength | Success on the same 80 goal episodes |
|---|---:|
| Original | 49/80 |
| Half strength | 59/80 |
| Full F | 68/80 |

These are diagnostic results, not independent validation.

### Independent practice validation
F was frozen before evaluation on **460 reserved variants**, subsequently tested with three seeds:

- **Overall:** 1261/1380 -> 1306/1380, or **91.4% -> 94.6%**
- **Paired gain:** **+3.26 percentage points**
- **Variant-clustered SE:** 0.81 points; approximate 95% CI **[+1.67, +4.85]**
- **Difficulty 5:** **59.5% -> 75.2%**
- **LIBERO Goal:** **77.4% -> 88.0%**

There were **53 recoveries and 8 regressions**; this is not a universal paraphrase fix.

### Safety
Across **1,536 paired trials** in the other six categories, overall successes were unchanged: **1282 -> 1282**. After deduplication, the largest category decrease was **0.42 points**.

All 50 observed canonical prompts avoid the edited rows. Moreover, **60 identical-input replays** spanning every category and suite produced **bit-identical actions and recorded activations**, including inputs from the discordant safety rollouts.

I expect this edit to help unseen paraphrases that use these lexical cues while preserving canonical-instruction behavior. The reported results are from practice variants; the benchmark held-out set remains unseen.

# Language robustness weight-edit experiment
## Constraints
No training, no kernel network execution; practice variants only. Use paired rollouts and independent validation. Budget: 50 forward passes.
## Current status
No edits. Inventory and matched-task diagnosis starting.

## Pass 1: diagnostic baseline
80 hard goal paraphrases, seed 7: 49/80 (61.25%); difficulty 3 18/19, 4 11/17, 5 20/44. Failures often replace canonical object names with synonyms/descriptions. Need separate lexical encoding from expert routing.

## Passes 2-5
Literal goal controls 9/10. Pass 5 diagnostic hard-language sample 102/128; goal 27/44 vs object 22/23, spatial 16/18, long 37/43. Expert attention is not absent on failing instructions; BOS is a strong sink. Will test sparse synonym-embedding canonicalization, protecting all canonical task token IDs.

## Candidate A: sparse unambiguous lexical aliases
cooker->stove, basin->bowl, cupboard->cabinet, grape/grapes/fermented/merlot->wine. 8 embedding rows; all 76 canonical task token IDs protected. First causal dose alpha=0.5. No other tensor changes.

## Candidate A, alpha=0.5 (passes 6-7)
Paired goal diagnostic rollout: +3.75 pp, SE 2.1, 3 recoveries / 0 regressions. 17/80 pairs had null terminations in both arms, so 63 valid pairs: 38->41 successes. Recovered IDs 1420 cooker, 1262 basin/cupboard, 1179 fermented grape. Probe 1420 expert L17 target cosine .594->.915; target initial xyz RMS .208->.069. 1262 expert L0 -.254->.755, L17 .103->.711; xyz RMS .100->.044. 1179 expert L0 .303->.788. Untouched prompt 1385 and 3 literal controls exactly unchanged. Now testing alpha=1.0.

## Candidate A alpha=1 (passes 8-9)
6 recoveries / 0 regressions (+7.5 pp over 80 listed; +10.17 pp, SE3.97 over 59 valid). 21 paired nulls. 1179 expert L17 target cosine .067/.393/.775 at doses 0/.5/1; xyz error .117/.104/.038. 1262 cosine .103/.711/.762. Best fallback saved in best_base/ and best_base_recipe.pt.
Candidate B adds descriptive cues at .75 strength, original aliases at 1.0; 48 rows. Generic container, dish, vessel, appliance, storage untouched.

## Candidate B (pass 10)
Diagnostic hard-language paired: 11 recoveries / 0 regressions, listed +8.6 pp SE2.5 (n128); {'valid': 91, 'total': 128, 'orig': 68, 'edit': 79, 'gain_pp': 12.09, 'se_pp': 3.44, 'WR': 11, 'RW': 0}. Runtime nulls verified as symmetric CUDA OOM, excluded from valid stats. Saved best_B/ and best_B_recipe.pt. Protecting canonical tokens gives exact literal-prompt invariance.

Pass 11 edited-only suffered 54/80 OOMs (20/26 usable successes). Compacting embedding artifact to float16 storage of exact bf16 inference values; no effective weight or inference setting change. Checking whether this reduces loader OOMs.

## Candidate B goal diagnostic (pass 12)
{'valid': 57, 'total': 80, 'orig': 34, 'edit': 48, 'gain_pp': 24.56, 'se_pp': 5.75, 'WR': 14, 'RW': 0}. 14 recoveries / 0 regressions. Compact file did not resolve OOMs; restored exact float32 artifact, only 48 selected rows changed. Preparing verb-alias extension as a separate test.

## Candidate C
Adds 25 verb-synonym embedding rows at .75 to candidate B. Motivation: residual slide/push, pull/open, secure/close primitive confusions. Canonical tokens remain protected; no action/expert weights changed.

## Candidate C (passes 14-15)
Broad diagnostic {'valid': 108, 'total': 128, 'orig': 87, 'edit': 100, 'gain_pp': 12.04, 'se_pp': 3.41, 'WR': 14, 'RW': 1}. Goal diagnostic: 49/80->69/80, +25.0 pp SE4.9, 20 recoveries, 0 regressions; no OOMs. Saved best_C/. Candidate now frozen for disjoint confirmation.

## Confirmation 1 (pass 16): C NOT CONFIRMED
128 entirely new variants: 104->106, +1.56 pp SE2.93, 8 recoveries/6 regressions. Object suite 23->20. This set is now development data; remaining 460 reserved variants are still untouched. Need ablate verb extension and examine ambiguous descriptive cues.

## Candidate D: semantic backoff after C failed confirmation
Remove heating->microwave, holder->rack, ceramic->mug, shut->close. Dairy becomes .5 original + .5 equal centroid(cheese,milk,butter), not cheese-specific. Woven->basket reduced to .25; round->bowl and flat->plate to .5. 66 rows, all canonical tokens still untouched. Will test known regressions and dairy-positive controls, then untouched confirmation 2.

## D targeted test (pass 17)

cases.prompt:
TASK. You are given the weights of pi0.5, a vision-language-action model (VLA) that controls a Franka robot arm in the LIBERO simulator (the released openpi checkpoint "pi05_libero", fine-tuned on the LIBERO demonstrations; it succeeds on ~96% of the original LIBERO tasks). Your job is to make it better at RECOVERING FROM FAILURES, by EDITING ITS WEIGHTS DIRECTLY. Each episode of the LIBERO-Recovery benchmark starts in the middle of a task, in a recorded state where a robot policy had already gone wrong (the grasp missed, the object was dropped or knocked over, an obstruction is in the way...). From there pi0.5 usually has every skill it needs to finish the task, yet it fails 40% of the time, and in about 80% of its failures it gets stuck in a RE-GRASP LOOP: it closes and opens the gripper again and again (6 or more flips) around the same place until the time limit, instead of adapting (e.g. moving to where the object now is). Find out what goes wrong inside the network in these episodes, identify the components responsible, and repair them with targeted changes, without hurting its ordinary task performance.

THE MODEL (3.62 B parameters; tensor names and shapes in NAMES / SHAPES).
- VISION: SigLIP So400m/14 ("paligemma_with_expert.paligemma.model.vision_tower.vision_model.*", 27 layers, width 1152) encodes each 224x224 camera image into 256 tokens; a linear projector ("...multi_modal_projector.linear") maps them to 2048.
- VLM: Gemma-2B ("paligemma_with_expert.paligemma.model.language_model.*", 18 layers, width 2048, 8 query heads and 1 KV head of dim 256, MLP 16384, embed_tokens 257152x2048) processes the prefix: 256 base-camera tokens, 256 wrist-camera tokens, 256 tokens of a masked-out third (empty) image, and the tokenized instruction (padded to 200 tokens). It builds a KV cache.
- ACTION EXPERT: Gemma-300M ("paligemma_with_expert.gemma_expert.model.*", 18 layers, width 1024, same head layout, MLP 4096) runs on 10 action tokens; in every layer its queries attend to the VLM's keys/values of the same layer (the prefix) and to the action tokens. Its RMSNorms are adaptive ("input_layernorm.dense", "post_attention_layernorm.dense", "norm.dense": Linear 1024->3072 conditioned on the flow-matching time). "action_in_proj", "action_out_proj", "time_mlp_in/out" map between the 32-d action space and width 1024. "gemma_expert.lm_head" is unused.
- INFERENCE: flow matching, 10 Euler steps from Gaussian noise, producing a chunk of 10 future actions (7-D: end-effector delta pose + gripper); the first 5 are executed, then the model is queried again. The robot state is NOT an input. The VLM prefix is computed once per query; the action expert reads it through attention at every denoising step.
- Inference runs in bf16 for most tensors (690 bf16, 122 fp32: layernorms, SigLIP embeddings, action heads); your edits are cast to each tensor's dtype, so changes much smaller than bf16 resolution (~0.4% relative) are lost.

THE BENCHMARK. LIBERO-Recovery (2026): failure scenes from the 4 LIBERO suites (spatial, object, goal, libero_10), each a recorded simulator state plus the original task instruction, labelled by recovery level: L1 retry (redo the failed grasp), L2 adapt (the situation changed; adjust the approach), L3 restore (an object was displaced/dropped and must be recovered first), L4 obstruction (something blocks the way). Every free object is shifted by a random +/-2 cm at the start (depends on the seed), and the gripper starts either open or closed ("grip"). An episode succeeds if the task's goal predicate holds within 520 policy steps (a few scenes are already solved at the start; they are reported separately). Baseline of this checkpoint on 440 episodes: 59.5% (L1 60, L2 72, L3 54, L4 53; libero_10 L3 17%); failures: 141/178 re-grasp loops, 27 wandering, 7 stalls.

HOW IT WILL BE MEASURED. After you finish, the edited and the unedited model are evaluated on HELD-OUT failure scenes you never see (a fixed half of all scenes, chosen by a hash), both gripper starts, fixed seeds: success rate (the goal: raise it) overall and per level, and the number of re-grasp-loop failures. Separately, ordinary performance on the original LIBERO tasks must not drop by more than ~2 points. Only weight values change: same tensor names and shapes, same inference code and settings.

WHAT COUNTS. Edits that come from understanding the network: find what drives the loop (e.g. which observation features or attention patterns keep the policy re-issuing the same grasp, whether the model "sees" that the object moved, how the gripper command is produced), localize the responsible components causally, and change them in a way you can justify with evidence. Out of scope: training of any kind; edits that only multiply a whole tensor by a constant; global changes to the noise or action scaling that are not tied to a mechanism.

WHAT YOU HAVE.
1. A persistent Python kernel (no internet, no GPU; CPU with many cores): variables survive between code blocks, like a notebook. Reply with exactly one block that starts with ```python to run code; if its last line is an expression its value is shown. One execution may take up to 900 s and 96 GB; output is cut at 10,000 characters; at most 300 code runs. Predefined: NAMES (all editable tensor names), SHAPES, load(name) (float32 torch tensor: your current edit if any, else the original), load_original(name), save_edit(name, tensor), drop_edit(name), edited() (names you edited), WORK (your read-write folder, kept for the whole run), and BENCH (read-only): BENCH/practice_scenes.json lists the PRACTICE failure scenes (id, scene_id, suite, level, stage, instruction, l4_injected) - the only ones you may run; the held-out ones are not listed. Gradients are disabled. The model's tokenizer is BENCH/paligemma_tokenizer.model (sentencepiece is installed: sentencepiece.SentencePieceProcessor(model_file=...)); openpi tokenizes the prompt as the cleaned instruction text followed by a newline ("\n"), with a BOS token. The instruction strings are in the rollout records; the token ranges of each query are in the probe outputs ("prefix_layout").
2. A forward-pass tool with a budget of 50 passes. Reply with exactly one block that starts with ```forward and contains JSON. Each request costs one pass:
 (a) ROLLOUT: {"type": "rollout", "model": "original" | "edited" | "both", "episodes": [{"id": <practice scene id>, "grip": "open" | "close", "seed": <int>}, ...] OR "sample": {"suite": optional, "level": optional ("L1".."L4" or a list), "stage": optional, "n": <number of scenes>, "seed": <int>, "grips": optional list (default both)}, "record": optional {"vlm_layers": [...], "expert_layers": [...], "vision_layers": [...], "what": "attn_out" | "mlp_out" | "resid"}, "save_frames": optional bool}. At most 256 episodes per pass ("both": at most 128 per model, run on the same scenes, grips and seeds, returning the paired difference with its standard error). Returns success (overall, by level, suite, stage and grip), re-grasp-loop counts, gripper-flip statistics; per-episode records in WORK/roll_<k>.jsonl (success, steps, grip_flips, frac_grip_closed, eef_path_m, eef_net_m, obj_deltas, path of the executed actions .npy); with "record", per-episode activation summaries (mean over the episode's policy queries; VLM outputs averaged separately over base-image, wrist-image and instruction tokens, expert outputs over the action tokens) as .npy in WORK/roll_<k>_acts/ with index.json; with "save_frames", the first observation and every 50th step as .png in WORK/roll_<k>_frames/ and the exact policy inputs needed for probes.
 (b) PROBE (cheap, no simulation): {"type": "probe", "model": "original" | "edited" | "both", "inputs": "<path of saved policy inputs from a rollout with save_frames, or a list of them>", "return": {"layers": [expert layers], "vlm_layers": [...], "vision_layers": [...], "what": "attn_out" | "mlp_out" | "resid" | "attn_maps"}}: runs the policy on stored observations (up to 512 inputs) and returns the predicted action chunk and requested activations (per call) as .npy in WORK/probe_<k>/ (attention maps of the action expert over the prefix: at most 4 inputs, at most 4 layers).
Same scene, grip and seed give the same episode (deterministic). A rollout pass of 256 episodes takes on the order of 10 minutes.

HOW TO WORK.
1. Diagnose first: compare looping failures with successful recoveries (and with ordinary episodes); look at the saved frames and action traces (where does it grasp, does it ever move toward the displaced object), and at which internal features or attention patterns differ.
2. Localize causally: correlation between a component and success is not enough; show that changing it changes the behaviour as predicted, with a dose-response.
3. Measure with power: success over n episodes has a standard error of about 50/sqrt(n) points. Compare original and edited on the SAME scenes, grips and seeds ("model": "both"), and keep an edit only if its gain is clearly larger than its standard error on scenes not used to choose it. Check for damage on scenes it already solves before you finish.
4. Plan your passes; keep WORK/notes.md up to date (findings with numbers, edits tried and their measured effect, current best edit; it is shown to you again if the conversation is restarted); keep copies of good edits (e.g. copy WORK/edited to WORK/best_1/).
5. Print compact summaries, never whole arrays; outputs are ASCII only.

RULES. Not allowed: (a) gradient descent or any training (no backward passes, autograd, optimizers, or iterative fitting of weights to a loss); (b) running the network yourself in the kernel on inputs (only the forward tool runs it); (c) reading benchmark files other than BENCH/practice_scenes.json (in particular not the held-out scene list) or anything outside WORK, BENCH and the weights; (d) internet access. Allowed: any analysis of weights and forward-tool results, any direct edit of weights that you compute and that is in scope.

HOW THE SESSION RUNS. It continues until all 50 forward passes are used; then make your final choice (the tensors in WORK/edited are submitted) and reply without a code block, saying what you changed, the evidence, and why you expect it to help.

cases.final_answer:
**Submitted: the original checkpoint, with no retained weight edits.** `/work/edited` has no active edits; I verified that the restored tensor exactly matches the original.

### Findings
Looping observations showed suspicious instruction fixation and visual/gripper-feedback patterns. Targeted head edits and rank-one interventions changed these internal signals, but **changing the suspected mechanism did not reliably improve recovery**. Several interventions instead damaged previously successful episodes, including at stronger doses.

### Decisive validation
The final frozen candidate modified only the action expert’s layer-17, head-1 output pathway. Across **288 valid paired episodes from 144 reserved practice scenes**:

| Metric | Original | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Successes | 166/288 (57.6%) | 164/288 (56.9%) |
| Re-grasp-loop failures | 98 | 98 |

The success difference was **−0.69 percentage points**, with scene-clustered SE **1.97 points**. There were **15 rescues but 17 losses**. Excluding already-solved starts did not change the conclusion. The positive result on the last panel did not outweigh the aggregate evidence.

### Final decision
The candidate failed every precommitted acceptance criterion, so I reverted it rather than submit an unsupported “repair.” **I did not establish a recovery improvement or conclusively localize a repairable causal fault.** Unchanged weights preserve the original policy; they are not expected to improve recovery.

The complete decision and validation statistics are saved in `/work/final_decision.json`, with investigation notes in `/work/notes.md`.
cases.notes:
# Recovery weight-edit investigation

## Protocol
- No training or kernel forward passes. Only permitted practice scenes.
- Scene-level discovery/validation split saved in scene_split.json before outcomes.
- Diagnose with actions, frames, attention, and activation/weight analysis.
- Require causal targeted ablations, dose-response, and paired validation.
- Ordinary-task evaluation is not explicitly exposed by the tool; check its availability, and do not substitute recovery preservation for ordinary-task evidence.

## Pass budget
- Forward passes used: 50/50. Final submitted edits: none.

## Current edits
- None. All candidates reverted; original checkpoint submitted.

## Pass 1: original, discovery, 128 paired-start episodes
- Success 71/128 (55.5%); L1 22/32, L2 21/32, L3 15/32, L4 13/32.
- Failures 57; re-grasp-loop failures 41; already-solved starts 7.
- Full expert attention-output summaries, selected VLM/vision summaries, actions and frames saved. No edits.

## Passes 2-4: initial probes
- Two matched task pairs: 367 (cream cheese/butter) and 753 (alphabet soup).
- BOS and wrist attention are common in both successes and loops; not enough for an ablation claim.
- Some mid-layer heads lose base-camera mass in looping observations; self-only heads also present.
- Collected all expert/VLM residual layers for 16 observations in four matched pairs.
- Important: final VLM block output is downstream of the last KV-cache creation; its large episode-level contrast is not itself a conditioning route.

## First causal candidate
- Expert L16 H3: average B/W/lang/self on two looping inputs 0.00/0.02/0.98/0.00 versus 0.01/0.35/0.65/0.00 on two matched successful inputs.
- Its raw gripper/pose readout coupling ratio is 1.386 (second highest across heads).
- Candidate E16H3_O_0.5: halve only columns 768:1024 of expert layer 16 o_proj. This is a targeted head ablation, not a whole-tensor or action rescaling.
- Screening panel fixed at 32 discovery scenes x both starts (baseline 31/64, 21 loop failures).

## Passes 6-7: E16H3_O_0.5 rejected
- Paired screen: 31/64 -> 29/64, -3.1 pp (SE 3.8), 2 rescues / 4 losses.
- Loop failures 21 -> 24; mean flips 12.52 -> 14.98.
- Contradicts simple excessive-prior interpretation; reverted.

## Pass 6 interpretation and next candidate
- E16H3 half-output: identical-input mean gripper differences only ~0.001, translation RMS changes 0.004-0.025. Raw output-weight alignment was not causal gripper evidence.
- Next: rank-one removal of a recorded wrist-minus-base key contrast from L10 H1 query, restricted to slow RoPE coordinate pairs. Probe must confirm the intended attention change.

## Passes 8-9: L10 H1 camera-direction removal rejected
- Probe: base mass in two loops rose 0.041->0.275 and 0.034->0.180; base-focused success 0.701->0.691. Action changes tiny (XYZ RMS ~0.001).
- Paired screen 31/64 -> 28/64, -4.7 pp (SE 3.5), 1 rescue / 4 losses; loops 21->22.
- Reverted; next isolated test is the same directional edit in spatial L12 H3.

## Passes 10-11: L12 H3 camera-direction removal rejected
- Base attention increased as intended; XYZ changes up to 0.017 RMS, gripper timing unchanged.
- Screen 31/64 -> 26/64, -7.8 pp (SE 4.0), 1 rescue / 6 losses, loops 21->23.
- Reverted. Evidence rejects a simple camera-rebalance repair in these two heads.
- Next diagnosis: visually encoded finger state versus action conditioning; saved state used only as an analysis label, never as policy input.

## Early gripper-state route hypothesis
- Open/closed t0 states differ mainly in fingers, but saved noises also differ: do not treat their expert residual contrast as purely visual.
- L0 H6 is the earliest strongly wrist-focused head (~82-90% wrist mass); L3 H2 and L15 H2 also focus on finger-region patches.
- Test partial L0 H6 O-block attenuation, using identical-input original/edited probes to identify actual gripper effects before evaluating it as a repair.

## Pass 12: L0 H6 half-output diagnostic
- 16 identical-input paired probes: 1/160 gripper signs changed; mean XYZ RMS 0.0072. Most gripper amplitude shifts ~0.03, not a timing repair.
- No rollout claim made; reverted to investigate actual gripper-decision route.
- Initial noise has only two arrays across discovery scenes, keyed by gripper start; this explains much of the very consistent expert initial contrast.

## Observational gripper check
- Across saved observations: Gaussian gripper-coordinate/output correlations 0.093 successes, 0.096 loops; finger-width/output correlations -0.567 successes, -0.636 loops.
- This supports strong visible-state dependence, not a globally noise-dominated gripper.
- Next localization: late finger-focused expert L15 H2 O block at 0.5.

## Pass 13: late finger head localization
- L15 H2 half-output: 2/160 gripper signs changed, both in input 13 (scene 1269, initially empty closed gripper); reopening delayed from token 2 to token 4.
- Other 15 inputs: action changes mostly ~0.001; downstream MLP responses partly cancel the head perturbation (L15 ~9-11%, L17 ~1-2%).
- Both early and late finger-head attenuation delay reopening in this state. Next test reverses the intervention: L15 H2 gain 2.0, to strengthen visual failed-grasp feedback.

## Pass 14: L15 H2 gain 2.0 not supported
- 17 paired inputs, including 8 empty-closed loops and 8 holding-like successes: no gripper sign changes, small pose changes. Original threshold case also unchanged.
- Reverted; no rollout claim. Continuing localization using actual residual increments and MLP outputs.

## Pass 15: visual-feedback localization
- Counterfactual fixed-noise copies were refused (no pass charged); only original rollout inputs used.
- Probed 24 matched t0 open/closed pairs; VLM residuals are independent of the differing action noise.
- Computing a matched visual gripper-state contrast, not a success/failure classifier or fitted weight model.
- Matched wrist residual contrast mean cosine across scenes ~0.50-0.57 in layers 0-13; two-half value-direction cosine ~0.72-0.83.
- Candidate: expert O projections at L1-14 attenuate only the corresponding one-dimensional visual gripper-state value direction by 50%, across heads. Directions orthogonalized to mean base/wrist/language values. No output/action/noise scaling.

## Pass 16: distributed visual-gripper attenuation probe
- 17 identical-input paired probes; 2/170 gripper signs changed.
- XYZ RMS change 0.0168.

## Pass 17: visual-gripper value attenuation rejected
- Fixed paired screen: 31/64 -> 25/64, -9.4 pp (SE 4.8), 2 rescues / 8 losses; loop failures 21 -> 23.
- This visual feedback is useful, not an expendable shortcut. Reverted attenuation.
- Next causal dose: gain 1.5 on the SAME protected value directions (alpha=-0.5), L1-14 expert O projections.

## Pass 18: visual-gripper value amplification rejected
- Same screen, gain 1.5: 31/64 -> 27/64, -6.2 pp (SE 3.8), 1 rescue / 5 losses; loop failures 21 -> 20.
- Both attenuation and amplification damaged solved scenes. Reverted all edits.
- Next hypothesis: action-token self-conditioning rather than inadequate raw gripper-state visibility.

## Self-conditioning hypothesis
- Saved maps: E15H5 ~100% action-token attention in all four matched observations; E16H0 ~98.6%, E16H1 ~99.8%, E16H5 ~99.6%; several E17 heads also ~100%.
- Grip-axis residual std in 48 t0 probes grows L14 12.8 -> L15 27.1 -> L16 50.0 -> L17 71.9 at first denoising call.
- Candidate E15H5_O_0.5: earliest isolated self-only head before this amplification. This is a causal test, not a claim that self-attention is inherently bad.

## Pass 19: E15H5 half-output probe
- 0/170 gripper signs changed; XYZ RMS 0.0039.
- E15H5 half-output probe: no sign changes; first-call downstream grip-axis RMS perturbation <0.75 vs natural signal std ~72. Reverted without rollout claim.
- Next: separate adaptive attention and MLP residual branches using identical-input recorded activations.

## Pass 20: adaptive branch decomposition
- Recovered observation-independent time/channel residual multipliers from recorded A, M, and residual increments; cross-observation reconstruction error at L14-17: 0.33%, 0.47%, 0.30%, 0.16%. Diagnostic algebra only; no weight fitting.
- First-call grip-axis increment std at L15/L16/L17: attention 8.00/9.67/16.23; MLP 5.14/11.26/8.72. Both branches matter.
- Adaptive gates substantially change head ranking: E15H4 gated grip/pose ratio 7.20 (highest inspected late head); E16H7 5.04, E15H2 4.85, E16H5 4.08. E16H3 raw alignment was misleading (gated ratio 0.52).
- Next candidate E15H4_O_0.5; mixed self/visual head with strong gripper-specific coupling.

## Pass 21: E15H4 half-output probe
- 0/170 gripper signs changed; XYZ RMS 0.0040.

## Pass 22: E15H4 half-output rejected
- Screen 31/64 -> 29/64, -3.1 pp (SE 3.1), 1 rescue / 3 losses; loops 21 -> 19 but mean flips increased 12.55 -> 13.69.
- Reverted. The previous probe panel was mostly saturated gripping states; next panel emphasizes predicted within-chunk transitions.

## Transition panel and sparse MLP feedback hypothesis
- Saved 64 transition-focused original inputs, 16 each loop/success x closing/opening, in transition_probe_manifest.json.
- Executed traces do NOT show higher approach speed at closing in loops: pre-close XYZ norm 0.333 loops vs 0.419 successes. No premature-speed claim.
- Candidate: halve 32 E16 MLP down-projection columns selected by gated gripper coupling and >4:1 squared grip/pose preference. No full-tensor scaling.

## Pass 23: E16 sparse MLP attenuation probe
- 32 channels contain 35.3% of gated grip coupling, 0.4% pose coupling; median input-grip-contrast alignment percentile 97.7%.
- Transition panel: 19/640 signs changed, 8/320 executed signs changed; XYZ RMS 0.0179.

## Pass 24: E16 MLP grip32 gain 0.5 rejected
- Paired screen 32/64 -> 27/64, -7.8 pp (SE 4.0), 1 rescue / 6 losses; loops 20 -> 23; mean flips 12.55 -> 14.56.
- Original result drifted by one success from earlier repeats (31 -> 32); always use the within-pass paired baseline.
- Attenuation destabilizes, contrary to an excessive-feedback account. Next fixed opposite dose: same 32 columns at gain 1.5.

## Pass 25: E16 MLP grip32 gain 1.5 rejected
- Screen 31/64 -> 29/64, -3.1 pp (SE 3.1), 1 rescue / 3 losses; loops 21 -> 20; flips 12.39 -> 13.36.
- Neither nonlinear-feedback dose improved recovery. Reverted.
- Next hypothesis: fully closed/empty-like hand cue is present visually but insufficiently coupled to corrective arm motion. Distinguish it from object-separated closed fingers and open hand, rather than weakening grasp commands.

## Pass 26: physical-state cue diagnosis
- Correct aperture is abs(q1-q2), not q1+q2 (opposite-signed finger joints).
- 15 fully-closed/empty-like, 16 holding-like, 16 open controls; derive/check split by scene hash.
- L15 value direction protected against holding/open/base/language means: held-out score means 0.608 empty, 0.228 holding, 0.149 open; pairwise separation 95.4%. Cue is not perfectly specific.
- Candidate: rank-one addition to E15H2 O block routes this visual cue toward upward reset. Other direct pose/grip readouts orthogonalized. beta=2 diagnostic, not yet evidence of recovery improvement.

## Pass 27: empty-cue retreat intervention probe
- fully_closed: actual attended cue mean 7.066; first-five mean Z action change 0.0123.
- holding_like: actual attended cue mean -1.440; first-five mean Z action change -0.0018.
- open: actual attended cue mean 0.155; first-five mean Z action change 0.0008.

## Pass 28: empty-cue upward retreat rejected
- Beta=2 paired screen: 31/64 -> 26/64, -7.8 pp (SE 3.4), 0 rescues / 5 losses.
- Loop failures 21 -> 23; mean flips 12.62 -> 14.64. Reverted.
- Visual selectivity and Z action causality did not imply a useful recovery behavior.
- Forward budget now 28/50; current edits none.

## Replanning-feedback diagnosis
- Future gripper prediction vs next executed chunk mismatch: 18.0% loop tokens, 10.8% success tokens (451/216 observations).
- Prefix-only attention maps imply E17H6 is almost wholly self-attending.
- E17H6 gated gripper coupling energy 1.382, versus 0.488 for E15H4 and 0.255 for E16H5; raw coupling alone was misleading.
- Causal candidate: halve E17H6 output block. Current edit E17H6_O_0.5, not yet evaluated.

## Pass 29: E17H6 half-output diagnostic
- Transition probe: 0/160 gripper signs changed; mean XYZ RMS about 0.016.
